notes: The default Sail CLI feature closure does not enable hyper tracing. The existing gate binary must not be assumed to emit hyper debug events merely because RUST_LOG mentions the module.
h2 control-frame modules log transmitted GOAWAY reason, RESET stream ID and reason, PING generation and PING acknowledgements. They exclude DATA and WINDOW_UPDATE frame logs.
Enable this filter on every peer and retain process/connection/endpoint identity; GOAWAY encoding itself records only the reason. RUST_LOG alone does not add missing addresses or task keys.

GOAWAY(NO_ERROR) is not proof of keepalive: the control establishes that a deliberately induced keepalive can produce it, and an identical outer Tonic body-read message can come from RST_STREAM(INTERNAL_ERROR).

Without hyper tracing, capture the complete server connection-future error to identify KeepAliveTimedOut directly. On the receiving body, induced keepalive mapped to Unknown/BrokenPipe while induced remote reset mapped to Internal/Reset.

The original unprefixed keepalive controls timed out because the initial proxy did not relay EOF after tokio::io::copy. Those logs/control-results.json are retained as fixture failures. The corrected-proxy and later runs explicitly call shutdown on the downstream write half.

The earliest isolated lock had five nontransport patch-version differences; Cargo.initial-control.lock preserves it. Current Cargo.lock aligns every dependency shared with Sail. All protocol packages were pinned from the first run.
All controls are local in-memory HTTP/2 peers; these are diagnostics controls, not a Sail reproduction, throughput result or distributed qualification.
